The Church holds both: justification is the free gift of grace, and we are created in Christ Jesus unto good works. Teach Ephesians 2:8–10 as one sentence, because that is how Paul wrote it.

ccc.q: no one can merit the initial grace of forgiveness and justification

chain.t: A man is justified by faith without the deeds of the law.
chain.s: Paul's subject: how a sinner is declared righteous.

chain.t: By the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.
chain.s: The negative stated as plainly as possible.

chain.t: Faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.
chain.s: James's subject: whether a claimed faith is alive.

chain.t: Shew me thy faith without thy works, and I will shew thee my faith by my works.
chain.s: Works are the evidence, not the payment.

chain.t: Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness.
chain.s: Both apostles quote the same verse, which proves they are not opponents.

chain.t: Faith which worketh by love.
chain.s: Paul himself says faith works. The debate was never faith against obedience.

items.christ: Notice the timeline and the whole thing settles. Abraham was counted righteous in Genesis 15, and the obedience James points to happens in Genesis 22 — about thirty years later. Paul describes how righteousness is received; James describes how it is recognised. Both are looking at the same Christ: one at what he gives, the other at what he produces. A tree is not made alive by its fruit, and a tree with no fruit was never alive.

items.q: How do I call people to obedience without turning the study into law?
items.a: Put the indicative before the imperative, as Scripture does. Tell them what God has done first, and let the command come as the natural response of people who already belong to him.
p: Notice the shape of the New Testament letters. Romans gives eleven chapters of what God has done before 'I beseech you therefore, brethren'. Ephesians gives three chapters of blessing before 'walk worthy'. The command always rests on the gift.

When a teacher reverses that order, obedience becomes the price of acceptance, and the hearers either despair or pretend. When the order is kept, obedience becomes gratitude, and people obey more, not less.
A simple test for your lesson: could a person leave knowing more about what God has done, or only about what he must do? If only the second, rewrite the opening.

ccc.q: Grace is favor, the free and undeserved help that God gives us to respond to his call to become children of God

chain.t: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God.
chain.s: Therefore. Eleven chapters of mercy come before the first command.

chain.t: I therefore… beseech you that ye walk worthy of the vocation wherewith ye are called.
chain.s: Three chapters of blessing precede walk worthy.

chain.t: The grace of God… teaching us that, denying ungodliness… we should live soberly.
chain.s: Grace is the teacher. Law never was.

chain.t: If ye love me, keep my commandments.
chain.s: Love first, obedience second, in the Lord's own order.

chain.t: We love him, because he first loved us.
chain.s: Everything we render back is a response to something already given.

items.christ: Keep God's order and obedience becomes gratitude. Reverse it and obedience becomes a price, and your hearers will either despair or pretend. Here is a simple test for your lesson: could a member leave knowing more about what God has done, or only more about what he must do? If only the second, you have taught law with Christian words. Put the mercies of God first, and watch how much more obedience follows.

items.q: A member says she has been praying for years and God is silent. What do I teach?
items.a: Do not explain God's reasons; you do not know them. Teach her that Scripture permits honest lament, that silence is not absence, and that faith holds on in the dark.
p: Scripture gives us the language for this and we should not be more pious than Scripture. How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever? That is in the Psalms, addressed to God, and it is prayer, not rebellion. Habakkuk complains. The Canaanite woman is met with silence and keeps asking, and the Lord commends her faith.
What we must not do is supply reasons God has not given: that there is hidden sin, that someone lacks faith, that a curse is operating. Job's friends did that and God rebuked them, not Job.
Stay with her. Encourage her to keep praying honestly, keep receiving the sacraments, and keep the company of believers. Silence endured in faith has made more saints than quick answers ever did.

chain.t: How long wilt thou forget me, O LORD? for ever?
chain.s: This is in the Bible, addressed to God. Honest lament is permitted.

chain.t: But I have trusted in thy mercy.
chain.s: The same psalm ends in trust. Lament is not unbelief.

chain.t: O LORD, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear!
chain.s: A prophet says it too.

chain.t: But he answered her not a word.
chain.s: The Lord was silent to a woman whose faith he then publicly praised.

chain.t: My wrath is kindled against thee… for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right.
chain.s: God rebukes the men who explained the suffering, not the man who suffered.

chain.t: He is faithful that promised.
chain.s: The ground of waiting is his faithfulness, not our feelings.

items.christ: There was one more silence, and it is the one that settles this. On the Cross the Son cried, my God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me — and heaven said nothing. He endured that silence so that it would never again mean rejection for us. So when a member tells you God is silent, do not supply reasons God has not given. Sit with her, keep her praying honestly, keep her in the sacraments and among believers, and tell her who else once waited in the dark and was heard.

items.q: If I preach grace strongly, will people not take it as licence to sin?
items.a: Some will twist it, as they did in St Paul's own day. His answer was not to preach less grace but to show that grace itself breaks sin's dominion.
p: Paul anticipated the objection and stated it himself: shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? God forbid. His argument is that the believer has died to sin in Christ, and that sin shall not have dominion over you, for ye are not under the law, but under grace.
Titus says the same thing positively: the grace of God that brings salvation teaches us to deny ungodliness and worldly lusts. Grace is not permission; it is power and it is instruction.

In practice, fear-based teaching produces outward conformity and inward resentment, while grace rightly taught produces love, and love obeys. Teach grace fully, and teach its consequences fully. Do not trim one to control the other.

ccc.q: The grace of Christ is the gratuitous gift that God makes to us of his own life

chain.t: Shall we continue in sin, that grace may abound? God forbid.
chain.s: Paul raises the objection himself, which means he was preaching grace strongly enough to provoke it.

chain.t: Sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace.
chain.s: Grace is given as the reason sin loses power, not as permission.

chain.t: The grace of God… teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly.
chain.s: Grace itself does the training.

chain.t: The motions of sins, which were by the law, did work in our members.
chain.s: The law stirred sin rather than stopping it.

chain.t: Use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh, but by love serve one another.
chain.s: Freedom is given a direction: love.

chain.t: Turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness.
chain.s: Scripture names the abuse — and still does not stop preaching grace.

items.christ: The answer to grace abused is not less grace; it is more Christ. A man who truly sees what the Cross cost does not go looking for how much he can get away with. Fear produces outward conformity and inward resentment; love produces obedience that no one is policing. Preach the whole of Romans 6 — dead to sin, alive unto God — and you will find your people sinning less than the congregation down the road that is being frightened weekly.

items.q: What is the difference between grace and mercy?
items.a: Grace gives what we have not earned; mercy withholds what we have earned. Both come from the same love of God and meet in the Cross.
p: Grace is favour: free, undeserved help given to us so that we may become children of God. Mercy looks at our misery and our guilt and does not give us what our sins deserve. Ephesians 2 puts them side by side: God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us, by grace ye are saved.
An illustration our people grasp quickly: if a man is guilty before a judge, mercy is the sentence not imposed, and grace is the judge then adopting him as his own son. The Gospel gives both.
Teach them together, because people who hear only mercy become passive, and people who hear only grace forget what they were spared.

ccc.q: Grace is favor, the free and undeserved help that God gives us to respond to his call

chain.t: God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us… by grace ye are saved.
chain.s: Both words in one sentence, both flowing from his love.

chain.t: Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us.
chain.s: Mercy is named as the motive of salvation.

chain.t: It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed… they are new every morning.
chain.s: Mercy withholds what we had earned, daily.

chain.t: That we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
chain.s: Obtain mercy for the failure, find grace for the need. Both at one throne.

chain.t: Where sin abounded, grace did much more abound.
chain.s: Grace is not merely equal to our sin; it overflows it.

items.christ: Both meet at one place. At the Cross, mercy withheld from us what our sins deserved, and grace gave us what we could never earn — the righteousness of the Son. That is why Hebrews sends us to one throne for both. Teach them together: a people who hear only mercy become passive, and a people who hear only grace forget what they were spared. Hold the two and you get worship.

items.q: Members are told their suffering proves a curse or hidden sin. How do I answer?
items.a: From Scripture, firmly. Hardship is not proof of God's anger, and Christ has redeemed us from the curse. Teaching that frightens suffering people is not the Gospel.
p: The Lord met this directly. The disciples asked who sinned that a man was born blind, and he refused the premise entirely before healing him. God rebuked Job's friends, who had spent chapters insisting that his losses proved hidden sin.

St Paul was shipwrecked, beaten and imprisoned, and he wrote much of the New Testament. Our Lord himself was a man of sorrows. If suffering proved rejection, Calvary would be unanswerable evidence against the Son of God.

So teach this plainly and often, because our people are sold fear constantly. Let them judge their circumstances by what the Cross says about God's love, and never judge God's love by their circumstances.

chain.t: Who did sin, this man, or his parents…? Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents.
chain.s: The Lord refuses the whole premise before he heals.

chain.t: Ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.
chain.s: God rebukes the men who read suffering as proof of sin.

chain.t: Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us.
chain.s: The curse was placed on him. It is not resting on you.

chain.t: He that spared not his own Son… how shall he not with him also freely give us all things?
chain.s: The Cross settles the question of God's disposition toward us.

chain.t: In stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent… thrice I suffered shipwreck.
chain.s: The most righteousness-conscious apostle suffered most.

chain.t: In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
chain.s: Trouble promised, and victory promised with it.

items.christ: Put the final answer where it cannot be argued with: Calvary. If suffering proved rejection, then the Son of God, a man of sorrows, acquainted with grief, would be the most rejected man who ever lived. The Cross makes nonsense of that arithmetic for ever. So teach your people to read their circumstances by what the Cross says about God's love, and never to read God's love by their circumstances. And when somebody tells a grieving member she is cursed, give her Galatians 3:13 and let her say it out loud.

items.q: If God is merciful, does sin still matter?
items.a: Yes. Mercy is not indifference. It is God dealing with sin at the greatest possible cost to himself rather than overlooking it.
p: The Cross is the answer to this question. God did not wave sin away; he bore it. Mercy that cost nothing would say nothing about how serious sin is; mercy that cost the life of the Son says everything.
This is why Scripture can hold together the God who is slow to anger and plenteous in mercy and the God who will by no means clear the guilty. Both are true, and they meet at Calvary.
Practically, teach repentance and mercy in the same lesson. A people who know how seriously God takes sin, and how completely he has dealt with it, are neither careless nor crushed.

chain.t: That he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus.
chain.s: God does not choose between justice and mercy. The Cross satisfies both.

chain.t: Merciful and gracious… and that will by no means clear the guilty.
chain.s: Both held together in God's own description of himself.

chain.t: He was wounded for our transgressions… the LORD hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.
chain.s: Sin was not overlooked; it was transferred.

chain.t: He hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin.
chain.s: The exchange that makes mercy righteous.

chain.t: Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other.
chain.s: The prophecy of exactly what happens at the Cross.

items.christ: Mercy that cost nothing would say nothing about how serious sin is. Mercy that cost the life of the Son says everything. That is why we can preach forgiveness without ever making light of sin: God took it so seriously that he bore it himself. Teach repentance and mercy in the same lesson, and your people will be neither careless nor crushed.

items.q: Our members attend for years and remain spiritual infants. What are we doing wrong?
items.a: Usually we are serving milk indefinitely, applying nothing, and never asking anyone to do anything. Maturity comes through the word applied and exercised, not through attendance.
p: Hebrews diagnoses it exactly: when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles. Strong meat belongs to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil. Note the phrase 'by reason of use'. Maturity comes from exercise.

So examine the session, not only the people. Does every lesson end with something specific to believe, change or practise? Does anyone ever ask next week what happened? Are we repeating the same comfortable themes because they are easy to teach?
Then plan a year, not a session. Decide where this community should be in twelve months and build the quarters toward it.

chain.t: When for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again.
chain.s: Time in church does not equal maturity. Scripture says so bluntly.

chain.t: Strong meat belongeth to them… who by reason of use have their senses exercised.
chain.s: By reason of use. Maturity comes through exercise, not attendance.

chain.t: For the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry… till we all come… unto a perfect man.
chain.s: Teaching exists to equip workers, not to entertain an audience.

chain.t: Be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
chain.s: Hearing without doing produces self-deception, which feels like growth.

chain.t: As newborn babes, desire the sincere milk of the word, that ye may grow thereby.
chain.s: Appetite for the word is the engine of growth.

items.christ: Then examine the session, not only the people. Does every lesson end with something specific to believe, change or practise? Does anyone ask next week what happened? Are we repeating the comfortable themes because they are easy to teach? And measure maturity the way Scripture does: not by how much a member knows, but by how much of Christ is being formed in him — until Christ be formed in you, as Paul puts it. Plan a year, not a session, and decide where this community should be in twelve months.

items.q: Are there levels or grades to attain in Christ?
items.a: There are no levels of acceptance before God — every believer stands on the same ground — but there is real growth in knowledge, character and usefulness.
p: Keep the two apart. In standing, there is one Lord, one faith, one baptism, and no believer is more accepted than another. In experience, Scripture plainly describes infants, young men and fathers, milk and strong meat, and commands us to grow in grace and in the knowledge of our Lord.

The distinction matters because teaching that offers spiritual levels usually offers them for a price: a special meeting, a particular man, an initiation. Our Lord rebuked his disciples every time they tried to rank themselves, and then washed their feet.
So press people to grow hungrily, and never let anyone be made to feel like a lower class of Christian.

chain.t: In him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. And ye are complete in him.
chain.s: Complete. There is no higher standing to attain.

chain.t: One body, and one Spirit… one Lord, one faith, one baptism.
chain.s: One, repeated seven times. No tiers.

chain.t: I write unto you, little children… young men… fathers.
chain.s: Real stages of growth, all inside the same family.

chain.t: Grow in grace, and in the knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ.
chain.s: Growth is commanded — in knowledge of a Person.

chain.t: Whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister.
chain.s: The Lord's answer to disciples arguing about rank.

chain.t: If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet.
chain.s: He settled the question of hierarchy with a towel.

items.christ: Keep standing and growth apart and everything becomes clear. In standing you are complete in him on your first day. In experience you grow all your life. The danger is that teaching which offers levels usually sells them: a special meeting, a mantle, an initiation, a particular man. Christ offers no such ladder — he offers himself, entire, to every believer. Press people to grow hungrily, and never let anyone in this parish be made to feel like a lower class of Christian.

items.q: A member asks how much he should pray and read to grow properly.
items.a: Give him a small rule he will actually keep every day rather than a large one he will abandon in a week. Faithfulness over time does what intensity in bursts never does.
p: Scripture speaks of meditating on the word day and night and of praying without ceasing, and both describe a settled habit rather than a heroic performance. The psalmist's tree is planted by rivers of water: it is the steady supply that makes the fruit.

Suggest something concrete: the Sunday readings during the week, ten minutes of Scripture, a decade of the Rosary or a few minutes of quiet prayer, and the Mass. Then let him add as it becomes natural.
Warn him gently against measuring his standing with God by his performance of the rule. The rule serves the relationship; it does not purchase it.

chain.t: His delight is in the law of the LORD… he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water.
chain.s: A steady supply, not an occasional flood, produces fruit.

chain.t: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.
chain.s: Meditation is a settled habit, not a heroic burst.

chain.t: They continued stedfastly in the apostles' doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.
chain.s: Four things together: teaching, fellowship, Eucharist, prayer.

chain.t: Pray without ceasing.
chain.s: A life turned toward God, not a quota of hours.

chain.t: Abide in me… without me ye can do nothing.
chain.s: The branch's work is to stay joined. That is the whole method.

items.christ: Give him a rule small enough that he will actually keep it — the Sunday readings through the week, a few minutes of Scripture, a little prayer, the Mass. Then warn him gently: the rule serves the relationship, it does not purchase it. A man who measures his standing with God by his performance of a devotional rule has quietly gone back under law. We abide in Christ; we do not earn him. The branch does not strain to produce grapes. It stays on the vine.

items.q: Is the Holy Spirit a Person or a power?
items.a: A divine Person, the third Person of the Blessed Trinity. He is not an impersonal force and not an atmosphere.
p: Scripture attributes personal acts to him throughout: he teaches, he bears witness, he intercedes, he forbids, he sends, he distributes gifts as he wills, and he can be grieved and lied to. None of these can be said of a force.

This is not an academic point. People who think of the Spirit as a power try to get more of it; people who know him as a Person listen to him and obey. Our language shapes our practice, so speak of him as 'he'.
It also protects the community. A Person can be grieved by how we behave in a meeting; a power can only be harnessed. That difference matters in a charismatic community.

ccc.q: it is Christ who is seen, the visible image of the invisible God, but it is the Spirit who reveals him

chain.t: I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter.
chain.s: Another of the same kind as Christ — therefore a Person.

chain.t: He will guide you into all truth… he shall not speak of himself.
chain.s: Guiding and choosing what to speak are acts of a person.

chain.t: The Holy Ghost said, Separate me Barnabas and Saul.
chain.s: He speaks, and he says me.

chain.t: Why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost?
chain.s: You cannot lie to a force.

chain.t: Grieve not the holy Spirit of God.
chain.s: Only a person can be grieved.

chain.t: The Spirit itself maketh intercession for us.
chain.s: He prays for us. That is a Person's work.

items.christ: And notice what this Person came to do: he shall glorify me, said the Lord. The Spirit is not a power to be harnessed for our purposes; he is a Person who has come to make Christ real to us and in us. So we do not try to get more of him — he is not a substance. We yield to him, listen to him and obey him. Speak of him as he, and your people's practice will change with your language.

items.q: How do we judge whether a manifestation is from the Holy Spirit?
items.a: By what it does with Christ, by its agreement with Scripture and the faith of the Church, by the order it keeps, and by the fruit it leaves behind.
p: Our Lord said the Spirit shall glorify me. St John tells us to try the spirits, and gives a doctrinal test about the confession of Christ come in the flesh. St Paul, writing to a very charismatic congregation, laid down rules of order precisely so that outsiders would be helped rather than confused.

So apply four tests: Does it exalt Christ or a personality? Does it agree with Scripture and with what the Church believes? Is it orderly, or does it trample the assembly? And what is left a month later — love, patience, self-control, or excitement and disorder?
Be neither credulous nor cynical. A ministry that tests nothing will be led astray; a ministry that welcomes nothing will quench the Spirit.

chain.t: He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you.
chain.s: Test one: does it exalt Christ or a personality?

chain.t: Every spirit that confesseth that Jesus Christ is come in the flesh is of God.
chain.s: Test two: the doctrinal confession about Christ.

chain.t: No man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost.
chain.s: The Spirit's fingerprint is the lordship of Jesus.

chain.t: God is not the author of confusion, but of peace.
chain.s: Test three: order, not uproar.

chain.t: The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering…
chain.s: Test four: what is left a month later.

chain.t: Quench not the Spirit… Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.
chain.s: Both commands together: do not quench, and do test.

items.christ: The four tests all converge on one question: where did this leave Christ? A manifestation that made a man famous, left a congregation frightened, and produced no love or self-control has failed, however impressive it looked. A quiet work that made people hungry for the Lord and gentler with each other has passed. Be neither credulous nor cynical: a ministry that tests nothing is led astray, and a ministry that welcomes nothing quenches the Spirit.

items.q: Is praying in tongues proof that someone has the Holy Spirit?
items.a: No. It is one gift among several, given as the Spirit wills. Nobody should be made to feel second-class for not having it, and nobody should be pressed into producing it.
p: St Paul asks plainly: do all speak with tongues? The expected answer is no. He also says the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal, and that the Spirit divides to every man severally as he will. The gifts are distributed, not uniform.

In our renewal this needs saying clearly, because the pressure is real. A believer who has never spoken in tongues is just as baptised, just as forgiven and just as indwelt. Love, not tongues, is the measure Paul gives.
Welcome the gift, teach its proper use, keep Paul's order in public gatherings, and never let it become a badge of rank.

chain.t: Dividing to every man severally as he will.
chain.s: The Spirit distributes. We do not all receive the same gift.

chain.t: Do all speak with tongues?
chain.s: Paul asks it expecting the answer no.

chain.t: The manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.
chain.s: Every believer is given something. Nobody is empty-handed.

chain.t: He that speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself.
chain.s: A real benefit, honestly stated.

chain.t: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass.
chain.s: Paul puts love above the gift he himself exercised most.

chain.t: If any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his.
chain.s: The possession of the Spirit, not a particular gift, marks a believer.

items.christ: This needs saying plainly in a charismatic community, because the pressure is real. A believer who has never spoken in tongues is just as baptised, just as forgiven, just as indwelt and just as loved. Welcome the gift, teach its proper use, keep Paul's order in the assembly, and refuse to let it become a badge of rank. The measure Paul gives is charity, and charity is Christ's own likeness being formed in us.

items.q: We are baptised and confirmed. What then is the 'baptism in the Spirit' people speak of in the renewal?
items.a: It is not another sacrament and it does not replace what Baptism and Confirmation gave. It is best described as a fresh stirring into life of the Spirit already given, so that what was received begins to be experienced and used.
p: Be careful and be accurate here, because this is where our renewal is most often misunderstood, inside and outside the Church. The Spirit is truly given in Baptism and Confirmation. Nobody who has been sacramentally initiated lacks the Holy Spirit.

What many describe is a release or awakening: the gift already given becoming conscious, active and fruitful, often with gifts of the Spirit following. The Acts of the Apostles shows the Spirit moving freshly on people who were already believers, and the early Church prayed for boldness and was filled again.

So teach it without competition between sacrament and experience. Avoid language that suggests Catholics receive the Spirit only at a prayer meeting. Avoid also the dead formalism that treats Confirmation as a leaving certificate.

chain.t: Ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you.
chain.s: Power for witness is the stated purpose.

chain.t: They were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness.
chain.s: The same people filled again — so a fresh filling is not a second conversion.

chain.t: Be filled with the Spirit.
chain.s: A continuous tense: go on being filled.

chain.t: Stir up the gift of God, which is in thee.
chain.s: Stir up what is already there. That is the language we should use.

chain.t: They sent unto them Peter and John… then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
chain.s: Believers already baptised receiving a further gift through the apostles.

chain.t: Received ye the Spirit by the works of the law, or by the hearing of faith?
chain.s: Whatever we receive, we receive by faith, not by performance.

items.christ: Speak of it as a release of what was given, not a competition between sacrament and experience. Avoid language that suggests Catholics only receive the Spirit at a prayer meeting, and avoid the dead formalism that treats Confirmation as a leaving certificate. And keep the purpose in view: the power is for witness, and the witness is to Christ. A filling that makes a man more spectacular but not more Christlike is not what Acts is describing.

items.q: Does crying in prayer always mean the Holy Spirit is at work?
items.a: No. Tears may come from the Spirit, and may equally come from grief, exhaustion, music or pressure in the room. Dry eyes are not a sign of a dry heart.
p: Scripture is full of tears and does not despise them: the Psalms, our Lord at the grave of Lazarus, St Paul serving the Lord with many tears. Nobody should be ashamed of weeping in prayer.
But tears are not the measure. The Lord's great prayer in John 17 records no tears at all. The Spirit's work is known by fruit and by agreement with the truth, not by how wet our faces are.

Watch the atmosphere in meetings. When music swells and a voice presses the congregation until people feel that nothing is happening unless they weep, that is pressure, not the Spirit, and the quiet ones go home feeling second-class.

chain.t: Jesus wept.
chain.s: The Lord himself wept, so tears are never despised.

chain.t: Who in the days of his flesh… offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears.
chain.s: Even his tears were real, not performed.

chain.t: Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son.
chain.s: The deepest prayer in Scripture, with no tears recorded.

chain.t: Elijah… said, LORD God of Abraham… Then the fire of the LORD fell.
chain.s: A few sentences, and fire fell. Volume is not the measure.

chain.t: The Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
chain.s: Genuine burdens do come, and should not be suppressed.

chain.t: Use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.
chain.s: The Lord warns against the very thing atmosphere produces.

items.christ: Judge prayer by its ground, not by its emotion. Did you come on the merit of the blood of Jesus? Did you speak honestly? Did you leave in peace? Then you prayed, wet-faced or dry. Watch the meeting where music swells and a voice presses until people feel nothing is happening unless they weep — that is pressure, not the Spirit, and the quiet ones go home feeling second-class. And if a member weeps constantly and carries a heaviness that will not lift, that may be grief or exhaustion rather than a spiritual matter, and there is no shame in talking to someone who can help.

items.q: A member feels his office job is less holy than ministry. Is he right?
items.a: No. Scripture addresses ordinary workers directly and tells them their work is service rendered to Christ. Most Christians are made holy exactly where they already are.
p: St Paul tells servants to do their work heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men, knowing that of the Lord they shall receive the reward. He tells the Thessalonians to study to be quiet, to do their own business and to work with their own hands. Our Lord himself spent most of his earthly life in a workshop.

The sacred-and-secular division does real damage here. It leaves people feeling that their daily life is spiritually empty and that only church activity counts, and it quietly excuses dishonesty at work because work is 'not spiritual'.
Teach the opposite: integrity in the office is worship, and the family at home is the first field of holiness.

chain.t: Whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.
chain.s: Whatsoever. The ordinary job is included by name.

chain.t: Ye serve the Lord Christ.
chain.s: The office worker is told plainly whom he is serving.

chain.t: Study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands.
chain.s: Quiet, ordinary labour is commanded, not tolerated.

chain.t: Is not this the carpenter?
chain.s: The Son of God spent most of his earthly life at a trade.

chain.t: That they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.
chain.s: Honest work makes the doctrine look beautiful. That is a witness.

chain.t: Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God.
chain.s: The widest possible statement, deliberately.

items.christ: The sacred-and-secular split does real damage: it leaves people feeling their daily life is spiritually empty, and it quietly excuses dishonesty at work because work is 'not spiritual'. Scripture says the opposite. Your member's integrity in the office is worship, his patience at home is holiness, and his diligence adorns the doctrine of God our Saviour. Christ himself sanctified ordinary labour by doing it for most of his life.

items.q: Members say they cannot evangelise because they are not preachers.
items.a: Witness is not preaching. It is a life people can read, and a simple account of your hope when someone asks.
p: St Peter does not tell ordinary believers to preach; he tells them to be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you, with meekness and fear. The manner is as much part of the instruction as the content.
St Paul calls believers a letter known and read of all men. In most of our families and offices, the life is read long before any word is accepted.
Give them something small and doable: one person to pray for, one invitation to make, one honest answer when asked. That is evangelisation, and the whole Church is sent to it.

pope.q: evangelization is first and foremost about preaching the Gospel to those who do not know Jesus Christ

chain.t: Be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear.
chain.s: An answer when asked — not a sermon when not asked.

chain.t: Ye are our epistle… known and read of all men.
chain.s: Your life is already being read, whether you speak or not.

chain.t: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father.
chain.s: The aim of visible goodness is that God gets the glory.

chain.t: One thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.
chain.s: The simplest testimony in Scripture, from a man with no training.

chain.t: Ye shall be witnesses unto me.
chain.s: Unto me. A witness testifies about a Person, not about a doctrine system.

chain.t: I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation.
chain.s: The power is in the message, not in the messenger's eloquence.

items.christ: Take the burden off them. They are not asked to win arguments; they are asked to tell what they know about Jesus and to live so that the telling is believable. The blind man had no theology and no training and his testimony silenced a council. Give each member one person to pray for, one invitation to make, and one honest answer when asked. That is evangelisation, and the whole Church is sent to it.

items.q: Which of our traditional customs may a Christian keep, and which must go?
items.a: Ask what the custom actually does. What is cultural — language, dress, food, music, respect for elders — can be kept and offered to God. What invokes another spiritual power, or binds a believer to it, must go.
p: The Church has never asked Africans to stop being African. The Gospel takes root in a culture and purifies it rather than erasing it. Our very motto is in our own language, and our worship is richer for it.

The line is drawn where a practice is an act of worship or allegiance to a spiritual power other than God: sacrifices and libations offered to spirits, consultations with diviners, charms worn for protection, oaths that bind a person to a shrine. Scripture is unambiguous about these, and no believer needs them, because Christ has disarmed every power.

Where a custom is doubtful, do not decide it alone and do not shame the person asking. Take it to the parish priest, and teach the principle so that members can reason it out for themselves next time.

pope.q: It is imperative to evangelize cultures in order to inculturate the Gospel.

chain.t: God hath made of one blood all nations… that they should seek the Lord.
chain.s: Every nation is God's making. Culture is not the enemy.

chain.t: A great multitude… of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues.
chain.s: Heaven is not culturally flattened. The nations arrive as nations.

chain.t: Ye cannot drink the cup of the Lord, and the cup of devils.
chain.s: The line is drawn at worship and allegiance, not at custom.

chain.t: There shall not be found among you… a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.
chain.s: Divination and consulting spirits are named and forbidden.

chain.t: Having spoiled principalities and powers, he made a shew of them openly, triumphing over them in it.
chain.s: A believer needs no charm, because the powers are already disarmed.

chain.t: Many of them also which used curious arts brought their books together, and burned them.
chain.s: The converts dealt with it themselves, publicly and decisively.

items.christ: So ask what the custom actually does. Language, dress, food, music, respect for elders — keep them, and offer them to God; our own motto is in our own tongue and our worship is richer for it. But where a practice is an act of worship or allegiance to another power, it must go, and not because the Church is foreign but because Christ has already won. A believer who truly sees Colossians 2:15 does not need a charm, and a believer who still wears one has not yet seen it. Where a case is doubtful, take it to the parish priest, and teach the principle so your members can reason it out next time.

items.q: I was invited to 'say a few words'. Am I to teach, preach, exhort or share?
items.a: Ask the person who invited you, before you prepare. Then do that one thing. Most failures in our meetings are a teacher doing the wrong one well.
p: The seven ways of handling the Word are not interchangeable. A teaching explains and orders truth. A homily or preaching proclaims Christ and calls for response. An exhortation encourages people to continue. A sharing lets everyone speak. Each has a different aim, a different length and a different shape.
So ask: how long, for whom, and what do you want them to leave with? Those three answers will tell you which of the seven is wanted.
If no one can tell you, choose exhortation. It is short, it is almost never wrong, and it does not pretend to be a lesson nobody asked for.

chain.t: Having then gifts differing… he that teacheth, on teaching; he that exhorteth, on exhortation.
chain.s: Scripture itself distinguishes teaching from exhortation.

chain.t: He that prophesieth speaketh unto men to edification, and exhortation, and comfort.
chain.s: Three different effects, named separately.

chain.t: Preach the word… reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering and doctrine.
chain.s: Even in one verse, different operations are listed.

chain.t: So they read in the book… distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand.
chain.s: That is a Bible study: read, explain, understand.

chain.t: Peter… lifted up his voice, and said unto them…
chain.s: That is preaching: proclaim and call for response.

chain.t: He exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they would cleave unto the Lord.
chain.s: That is exhortation: come alongside and strengthen.

items.christ: Ask the host three questions before you prepare: how long, for whom, and what should they leave with? Those answers tell you which of the seven is wanted. And whichever one it is, the aim does not change. A teaching should leave them understanding Christ better; a homily should leave them responding to Christ; an exhortation should leave them continuing in Christ. Different roads, one destination.

items.q: Someone asks a question in the hall and I do not know the answer. What do I do?
items.a: Say so, write it down, and bring the answer next week. A teacher who admits a limit keeps his credibility; one who improvises loses it the first time he is checked.
p: Nothing damages a teaching ministry faster than confident invention. Our people can now check anything on a phone, and once a teacher has been caught making up an answer, his sound teaching is doubted too.

So have a formula ready: 'That is a good question and I will not guess at it. Let me study it and bring it back next week.' Then actually bring it back, even if the answer is that the Church permits different opinions.
Take difficult questions to the priest, to this committee, or to the readiness checklist process. That is partly what the committee exists for.

chain.t: The heart of the righteous studieth to answer: but the mouth of the wicked poureth out evil things.
chain.s: Studying before answering is called righteousness here.

chain.t: He that answereth a matter before he heareth it, it is folly and shame unto him.
chain.s: Answering too quickly is named folly.

chain.t: They searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.
chain.s: Your hearers are meant to check you. Plan for it.

chain.t: Knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation.
chain.s: A sober reason not to invent.

chain.t: Not handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves.
chain.s: Honesty is itself part of the commendation.

items.christ: Have the sentence ready before you need it: that is a good question, and I will not guess at it; let me study it and bring it back next week. Then actually bring it back, even if the answer is that believers may hold different views. Nothing destroys a teaching ministry faster than confident invention, and nothing builds trust faster than a teacher who can say I do not know. You are not the source; you are a servant of the Word. The Lord is not diminished when his servant admits a limit.

items.q: Another teacher taught something I believe is wrong. What do I do?
items.a: Go to him privately, with the text open, and ask how he reached it. Correct from Scripture, not from reputation, and keep it out of the hall unless the error is serious and public.
p: The aim is the truth and the brother, not a victory. Our Lord's own instruction is to go first privately. St Paul did withstand St Peter publicly, but that was a public act with public consequences for the Gospel itself, not a difference over a detail.

Separate the three cases before acting: a plain error of fact, a matter where believers may legitimately differ, and a teaching that damages souls — fear teaching, curse doctrines, or anything that contradicts the faith. Only the third needs urgency, and the parish priest should know about it.
And accept the same treatment yourself. A teacher who cannot be questioned has become the problem he is meant to prevent.

ccc.q: Read the Scripture within "the living Tradition of the whole Church"

chain.t: Go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone.
chain.s: Private first. The Lord's own instruction.

chain.t: I withstood him to the face… before them all.
chain.s: Public correction, but for a public act that struck at the gospel itself.

chain.t: The servant of the Lord must not strive… in meekness instructing those that oppose themselves.
chain.s: The manner is commanded as firmly as the correction.

chain.t: Speaking the truth in love, may grow up into him in all things.
chain.s: Truth and love together, and the aim is growth into Christ.

chain.t: Open rebuke is better than secret love. Faithful are the wounds of a friend.
chain.s: Correction given well is a kindness, not an attack.

chain.t: Him that is weak in the faith receive ye, but not to doubtful disputations.
chain.s: Some matters are genuinely open. Do not fight over those.

items.christ: Sort it into three before you move: a plain error of fact, a matter where believers may differ, or a teaching that damages souls — fear doctrine, curse teaching, anything contradicting the faith. Only the third needs urgency, and the priest should know. Go with the text open and ask how he reached it, rather than telling him he is wrong. And accept the same treatment yourself: a teacher who cannot be questioned has become the very problem he was ordained to prevent.

items.q: One member takes over every session with long stories. How do I handle it?
items.a: Handle it in the structure, not in a confrontation. Set the time rule for everyone at the start, use direct questions to bring others in, and speak to him privately and kindly afterwards.
p: Announce the rule before it is needed: we will hear three or four people on this question, two minutes each, so that everybody has a turn. A rule given to the whole group is not an attack on anyone.
Then use the facilitator's tools: thank him, summarise his point in one sentence, and ask a different person by name. Return to the text: 'let us see what verse 14 says about that.'
Afterwards, thank him privately for his willingness to speak and ask for his help in drawing out the quieter members. Many dominant talkers respond very well to being given that responsibility.

chain.t: Let the prophets speak two or three… ye may all prophesy one by one, that all may learn.
chain.s: Paul limits speakers so that all may learn. Structure is apostolic.

chain.t: Let all things be done decently and in order.
chain.s: Order is not unspiritual; it is commanded.

chain.t: Swift to hear, slow to speak.
chain.s: The rule for everyone in the room, including the teacher.

chain.t: In the multitude of words there wanteth not sin.
chain.s: Long speech has its own dangers.

chain.t: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.
chain.s: Yielding airtime is an act of love.

items.christ: Handle it in the structure, not in a confrontation. Announce the rule before it is needed — three or four speakers, two minutes each, so everyone has a turn — because a rule given to the whole group is not an attack on anyone. Thank him, summarise his point in one sentence, ask someone else by name, and return to the text. Afterwards, thank him privately and ask for his help in drawing out the quiet members. Many dominant talkers respond beautifully to being given that responsibility, because what they actually wanted was to matter.

items.q: Is it not better to depend on the Holy Spirit than to over-prepare?
items.a: That is a false choice. Preparation is one of the ways the Spirit works, and claiming his leading as a cover for laziness dishonours him.
p: Ezra prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments. St Paul tells Timothy to study to show himself approved, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth. Those are commands about work.

The Lord's promise that the Spirit would give words in the hour of need was given about being dragged before rulers and magistrates, not about a scheduled Thursday Bible study you have known about for a month.
Prepare thoroughly, then hold the plan loosely in the room. The Spirit leads in the preparation and in the delivery.

chain.t: Ezra had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel.
chain.s: Prepare, seek, do, teach — in that order.

chain.t: Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed.
chain.s: A workman. Teaching is work.

chain.t: When they bring you unto the synagogues… the Holy Ghost shall teach you in the same hour.
chain.s: The promise is about being dragged before rulers, not a scheduled class.

chain.t: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.
chain.s: Diligence and haste are contrasted plainly.

chain.t: Give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine… meditate upon these things; give thyself wholly to them.
chain.s: Paul tells a Spirit-filled young minister to study hard.

items.christ: The Spirit leads in the preparation as truly as in the delivery. Prepare thoroughly, then hold the plan loosely in the room. And remember who you are preparing to present: you are not preparing a performance, you are preparing to show people Christ out of the Scriptures. That is worth a week of work. Claiming the Spirit's leading as cover for laziness does not honour him; it uses his name to excuse what we did not do.

items.q: May I teach from a vision, dream or personal encounter?
items.a: You may tell it as testimony. You may not build teaching on it. Doctrine comes from Scripture and the faith of the Church, because that is what the hearers can check.
p: St Peter had stood on the holy mount and heard the voice from heaven, and still directed his readers to the more sure word of prophecy. If his experience was not the foundation, ours is not either.

The practical danger is accountability. If I teach from Scripture, you can open the book and test me. If I teach from what I was shown, you must either accept it or be accused of doubting God. That is how control begins and how fear spreads through a parish.
The Church is careful here for the same reason: private revelation, even when genuine, does not add to the faith given once for all. Tell your testimony gladly, and let the lesson rest on the word.

chain.t: We were eyewitnesses of his majesty… this voice which came from heaven we heard.
chain.s: Peter had the strongest possible experience.

chain.t: We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed.
chain.s: And he still calls the written word more sure.

chain.t: Though we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel… let him be accursed.
chain.s: Even an angelic encounter does not outrank the gospel already given.

chain.t: Intruding into those things which he hath not seen, vainly puffed up… and not holding the Head.
chain.s: Scripture names this error precisely, and says it loses hold of Christ.

chain.t: Prove all things; hold fast that which is good.
chain.s: Everything is to be tested, including our own experiences.

chain.t: To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word… there is no light in them.
chain.s: The standard of testing is the word itself.

items.christ: The practical danger is accountability. If I teach from Scripture, you can open the book and test me. If I teach from what I was shown, you must either accept it or be accused of doubting God — and that is how control begins and how fear spreads through a parish. Tell your testimony gladly; it is yours and it is real. But build the lesson on the word, which belongs to everybody, and which always leads to the same Christ.

items.q: Is it true that judgment must begin at the house of God?
items.a: The sentence is in Scripture, in 1 Peter 4:17. But Peter wrote it to comfort a Church under persecution, not to frighten a congregation. The judgment he means is the fiery trial they were already passing through.
p: Read the paragraph it sits in. From verse 12 Peter says: beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you. He is writing to believers scattered and suffering for the name of Christ, and he tells them their suffering is not a sign of God's anger but a share in the sufferings of Christ. Then comes verse 17: the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God.

The word carries the sense of a sifting and refining that starts with God's own household. Peter's argument runs from the lesser to the greater: if God permits his own people to be tried like this, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God? The verse was written to steady frightened believers, and it ends in verse 19 with the exact opposite of terror — let them that suffer commit the keeping of their souls to him in well doing, as unto a faithful Creator.

There is an Old Testament shape behind it. In Ezekiel 9:6 the command is to begin at the sanctuary, and in Jeremiah 25:29 God begins with the city called by his name. God does deal first with his own household. That is a serious thing, and we should not soften it.

But notice what happens when the sentence is lifted out and used as a weapon. A preacher quotes six words, the congregation is frightened, and the money or the behaviour follows. That is the reverse of what Peter was doing. He said do not think it strange, and the man quoting him makes people think of nothing else. Teach the whole paragraph, verses 12 to 19, and the fear goes while the seriousness stays.

ccc.q: to the content and unity of the whole Scripture
ccc.note: the first criterion: no sentence is read apart from the whole

chain.t: Think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you.
chain.s: The subject of the paragraph is persecution, set out five verses earlier.

chain.t: Rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ's sufferings.
chain.s: Their suffering is a share in his, not a punishment from him.

chain.t: The time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God.
chain.s: The sifting Peter means is the trial they are already in.

chain.t: Let them… commit the keeping of their souls to him in well doing, as unto a faithful Creator.
chain.s: The paragraph ends in confidence, not terror.

chain.t: Begin at my sanctuary.
chain.s: The Old Testament shape: God deals first with his own house.

chain.t: There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus.
chain.s: Whatever this judgment is, it is not condemnation for those in Christ.

items.christ: The whole thing turns on one distinction: sifting is not condemnation. Christ bore the condemnation at Calvary; nothing is left of it for those who are in him. What remains for the household is a refining that produces gold, and Peter wrote about it to steady frightened people, not to frighten steady ones. So teach verses 12 to 19 together. The fear goes and the seriousness stays, which is exactly what Peter intended.

items.q: Will teachers be the first to be judged?
items.a: Scripture does not say first. James 3:1 says teachers are judged by a stricter standard, which is a different thing. The word first comes from 1 Peter 4:17, and the two verses are being fused into a sentence neither of them contains.
p: Take James on his own. My brethren, be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation. The older English word masters means teachers, and the greater condemnation means a stricter judgement, a higher standard of account. James says nothing about order or timing. He says the standard is higher.

Then read the next verse, because James did not stop at a warning. For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man. His whole argument in chapter 3 is about the tongue. Teaching is done with the tongue, the tongue is the hardest member to govern, so do not rush into the work. He is warning against a crowd of eager, unprepared teachers — which is exactly what a teaching ministry should be careful about.

Now notice the fusion. Somebody takes first from Peter, takes teachers from James, and produces: teachers will be the first to be judged. That sentence is in no Bible. This is the ordinary way error is made here — two true verses welded into a third statement that neither says. The Church's own rule of interpretation is the coherence of the truths of faith with one another, and a conclusion welded out of two unrelated passages fails that test.

What should this do to you as a teacher? Sober you, not paralyse you. James said be not many teachers; he did not say be no teachers, and he went on teaching himself. Prepare properly, show your working from the text, take correction, and let your life agree with your lesson. A teacher who does that has nothing to dread. A teacher who uses the verse to frighten other people, while refusing correction himself, has misunderstood it twice.

ccc.q: the coherence of the truths of faith among themselves and within the whole plan of Revelation
ccc.note: the analogy of faith: a conclusion welded from two unrelated verses fails it

chain.t: Be not many masters, knowing that we shall receive the greater condemnation.
chain.s: A stricter standard. Nothing about order or timing.

chain.t: For in many things we offend all. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man.
chain.s: The very next verse explains why: this is about the tongue.

chain.t: The tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things… the tongue is a fire.
chain.s: Chapter 3 is a chapter about speech, and teaching is speech.

chain.t: Judgment must begin at the house of God.
chain.s: Here is where the word 'first' comes from — a different writer, a different subject.

chain.t: Rightly dividing the word of truth.
chain.s: The remedy for welding two verses together is dividing them rightly.

chain.t: No condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus.
chain.s: The teacher stands in Christ like every other believer.

items.christ: Two true verses were welded into a third statement that neither contains. Teach your people to see that move, and they will catch it everywhere. Then let the warning land where James put it: be careful with your tongue, prepare properly, show your working, take correction, and let your life agree with your lesson. A teacher who does that has nothing to dread — his standing is in Christ, exactly like the newest member of his class. The higher standard is on his work, never on his welcome.

items.q: Why do Catholics pray to Mary and the saints? I am asked this constantly.
items.a: We do not worship them; we ask them to pray for us, as we ask one another. Worship belongs to God alone, and every grace comes through Christ, the one Mediator.
p: Begin with what we agree on, because the questioner usually assumes we deny it: there is one God and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus. The Church teaches exactly that.

Then explain what asking the saints actually is. We ask fellow Christians to pray for us all the time, and Scripture commends it. Those who have died in Christ are alive in him, and the great cloud of witnesses surrounds us. Asking their prayers is the same act, not a different one.

Honour given to Our Lady is not the worship given to God, and she herself directs attention away from herself: whatsoever he saith unto you, do it. Answer calmly, make the distinction clearly, and do not let the conversation drift away from Christ, which is usually where it was headed.

chain.t: There is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.
chain.s: Start where you agree. The Church teaches exactly this.

chain.t: Pray one for another… the effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.
chain.s: Asking another believer to pray is commended, not forbidden.

chain.t: We also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses.
chain.s: Those who have gone before are not absent or inactive.

chain.t: He is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him.
chain.s: Those in Christ are alive, which is why asking their prayers is not a seance.

chain.t: All generations shall call me blessed.
chain.s: Scripture itself says this will happen.

chain.t: Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.
chain.s: Our Lady's last recorded words point away from herself to her Son.

items.christ: End it where she ends it. Her last recorded words in Scripture are an instruction to do whatever Jesus says, and that is the whole posture. Honour given to her is not the worship given to God, and every grace comes through the one Mediator. Make the distinction calmly, agree loudly on 1 Timothy 2:5, and then steer the conversation to Christ — which, if you listen carefully, is usually where the questioner wanted it to go anyway.

items.q: Why confess to a priest when I can confess directly to God?
items.a: We do confess directly to God, and the sacrament is how he gives us his forgiveness audibly through the ministry he established. Christ gave that ministry to the Church himself.
p: The Church's teaching rests on the Lord's own words after the Resurrection: whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them. He entrusted a ministry of reconciliation to his apostles, and St Paul says God has given to us the ministry of reconciliation.
St James tells believers plainly to confess their faults one to another and pray one for another. Christianity is not a private transaction; grace comes through the Body of Christ.

And there is a pastoral reason our people feel immediately: it is one thing to hope you are forgiven, and another to hear it said to you. Many Catholics carry forgiven sins for years precisely because they never heard absolution spoken.

chain.t: As my Father hath sent me, even so send I you… Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted.
chain.s: The risen Lord entrusts a ministry of forgiveness to men.

chain.t: God… hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation.
chain.s: Paul says the ministry was given, not merely the message.

chain.t: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed.
chain.s: Confession in Scripture is not a private transaction.

chain.t: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us.
chain.s: God is the forgiver in every case. The priest is never the source.

chain.t: They glorified God, which had given such power unto men.
chain.s: The crowd's own reaction when Christ forgave sins through a man's mouth.

items.christ: Keep the source clear and nobody can misunderstand you: it is Christ who forgives, always and only. The priest speaks his word, and that is the mercy of it — a Catholic does not have to hope he is forgiven, he hears it said to him. Many of our people carry forgiven sins for years because they never heard absolution spoken aloud. That is a pastoral tragedy, not a doctrinal one, and the remedy is at hand.

items.q: A member asks whether our Pentecostal friends and relatives are saved.
items.a: Do not answer that about any individual; it is God's judgement, not ours. Teach what salvation is, honour the real faith we see in other Christians, and keep the conversation on Christ.
p: The question is usually asked in a spirit of rivalry, and we should refuse that spirit. Baptised Christians outside the full communion of the Catholic Church are our brothers and sisters, and we recognise genuine faith, genuine love for Scripture and genuine fruit among them. We have things to learn from their hunger for the word.

What we hold, and should be able to explain without insult, is that Christ willed one Church and entrusted to her the fullness of the means of grace. Saying that is not the same as pronouncing on who is saved, which nobody has authorised us to do.
Teach our members to stop competing and start being taught. A Catholic who knows his Bible and loves Christ ends these arguments simply by existing.

chain.t: Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name… Forbid him not: for he that is not against us is on our part.
chain.s: The Lord rebukes the rivalry instinct directly.

chain.t: That they all may be one… that the world may believe.
chain.s: Christ's own prayer, and his stated reason: the world's believing.

chain.t: One body… one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all.
chain.s: What we hold in common with every baptised Christian.

chain.t: I am of Paul… Is Christ divided?
chain.s: Party spirit was condemned in the first generation.

chain.t: Who art thou that judgest another man's servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth.
chain.s: Judging individuals is explicitly taken out of our hands.

chain.t: Christ is preached; and I therein do rejoice.
chain.s: Paul's own posture when others preached with mixed motives.

items.christ: Refuse the competition. We recognise genuine faith and genuine love for Scripture among our separated brethren, and we have things to learn from their hunger for the word. What we hold, and should be able to explain without insult, is that Christ willed one Church and entrusted to her the fullness of the means of grace — which is not the same as pronouncing who is saved, a judgement nobody has authorised us to make. Teach our members to stop arguing and start being taught. A Catholic who knows his Bible and loves Christ ends these arguments simply by existing.

items.q: What do I say about teaching that wealth proves God's favour and poverty proves a curse?
items.a: Say that Scripture does not teach it. God does bless, and money is not evil, but prosperity is never given as the measure of his favour, and our Lord and his apostles would fail that test.
p: Look at who Scripture calls blessed. Our Lord had nowhere to lay his head. St Paul knew both how to be abased and how to abound. The rich man in the parable was not commended for his barns. Meanwhile the Psalms wrestle openly with the fact that the wicked often prosper.
Scripture does warn clearly about teachers who suppose that gain is godliness, and about those who through covetousness make merchandise of the faithful. That is a word for us, not only about others.
Teach honest work, generosity, contentment and the care of the poor, and refuse the arithmetic that reads a person's bank balance as a verdict from God.

chain.t: Supposing that gain is godliness: from such withdraw thyself.
chain.s: Scripture names the error and tells us what to do about it.

chain.t: They that will be rich fall into temptation… the love of money is the root of all evil.
chain.s: Not money; the love of it.

chain.t: I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound.
chain.s: Paul fails the prosperity test, and he wrote half the New Testament.

chain.t: I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked… until I went into the sanctuary.
chain.s: Scripture wrestles openly with the wicked prospering.

chain.t: The Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
chain.s: The Lord himself would fail the test.

chain.t: Though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might be rich.
chain.s: The real exchange, and the riches it actually means.

items.christ: The last verse is the answer. Christ's poverty purchased riches for us — and Paul explains in the same letter what those riches are: grace abounding, every good work supplied, a life enriched to be generous. God does bless, money is not evil, and honest work and generosity are commanded. But the arithmetic that reads a bank balance as a verdict from God collapses at the manger and the Cross. Teach contentment, diligence, generosity and the care of the poor, and your people will be richer than the ones being charged for breakthroughs.

site.welcome: Welcome to the Teaching Ministry. Everything our committee has prepared for the year is here: the Bible study for the whole community, the formation of our teachers, the workshops, and the answers to the questions we are asked in the hall. Open it, use it, and teach Christ.
site.guiding: What does this passage reveal about God, His redemptive purpose, and Christ — and how should that truth shape the believer's life?
howto: Begin with the Key Scripture and read the passage in context.
Use the Teaching Focus / HINT as the controlling idea of the lesson.
Allow the main text to lead the discussion before moving to supporting Scriptures.
When using another Scripture to explain the passage, explain the connection rather than simply quoting isolated verses.
End with application: what should we believe, change, practise, avoid or become because of what Scripture teaches?
Use the questions and answers to anticipate what people will ask and to stimulate discussion.

insider.intro: A teacher stands before the meeting for approximately 40 minutes to teach a selected topic, especially where there is a need for clear biblical understanding of doctrine, difficult passages, Christian identity, salvation, grace, faith, the Holy Spirit, the Church or Christian living.
insider.purpose: A focused Bible teaching session in which the teacher explains Scripture carefully, allows Scripture to explain Scripture, and points the teaching to Christ.

segments.d: State the topic, why it matters and the central question.
Read and explain the principal passage in context — author, audience, setting, argument and key words where relevant.
Bring in supporting passages that clarify, balance or develop the main text. Explain the connection.
Show how the teaching points to Christ, His work, His character, His lordship or life in Him. Apply the truth to Christian living.
Restate the main truth, give practical responses and take questions.

standard.purpose: Keep the Bible itself as the authority for the teaching.
standard.body: Teach the Bible, not merely your opinion about the Bible. Start with what the text says. Explain it in context. Compare Scripture with Scripture. Keep Christ central. Where a doctrine is disputed, state clearly what the text supports and avoid claiming certainty beyond Scripture.

How to interpret difficult passages without taking verses out of context.

Spiritual maturity, perseverance and the Christian's hope of glory.

philosophy: Teachers within the fellowship should normally teach the workshop. This keeps teachers proactive, prepared and continually studying.
A sound guest teacher may be invited when appropriate. A guest should be sound in Scripture and competent in the subject being addressed.

The workshop should be more in-depth than weekly Bible sharing. It may include context, word studies, comparison of passages, doctrinal positions, case studies, teaching practice and extended questions.
Every teacher remains a learner. Preparation should involve prayerful study, reading, cross-referencing and the ability to explain conclusions from Scripture.
The goal is multiplication. The workshop should develop teachers who can teach others clearly and faithfully.
checklist: Have I prayed and prepared my heart?
Have I read the main passage in context?
Can I state the central truth in one sentence?
Do my supporting Scriptures actually support the point?
Have I considered the immediate and wider biblical context?
Can I show how the teaching points to Christ?
Can I distinguish Scripture from my interpretation or opinion?
What questions or objections may arise?
What should the learner believe, change or practise?

culture.purpose: Develop teachers who are continually ready to study and serve.
culture.body: We want teachers who are always ready — ready to study, ready to explain Scripture, ready to answer with humility, ready to be corrected by Scripture, and ready to help another teacher grow. The aim is not to create impressive speakers, but faithful servants who handle God's Word carefully and point people to Christ.

Members are asked to study the topics first, on their own or in their Bible study group, and then come to the training where each subject is taught in full and questions are taken. The ministry is ready to run this for any member, any group or any ministry that asks, and we recommend it for all our ministers. Speak to the Bible Study Committee to fix the dates.

caveat.lead: What is published here is the syllabus, not the teaching.
p: Each class gives you the subject, its key Scripture and what the class is meant to achieve. It does not give you the lesson written out. That is deliberate: this is a training curriculum, and the teaching itself is given live, by a teacher, in the ministry's training sessions.

So it is used in two steps. First you study: take the subject and the Scripture and work through them yourself, or in your Bible study group, before you come. Then you are trained: the ministry teaches each subject in full over a set number of days, takes your questions, and forms you as a facilitator.
The ministry is ready to run this training at any time — for a single member who wants to go through it, for a group, or for a whole ministry that asks for it. We recommend it for all our ministers.
caveat.short: Syllabus, not the full lesson. Each class gives the subject, the Scripture and the aim; the teaching itself is given live in the ministry's training sessions.

steps.d: Take the subject and the key Scripture of each class and work through them in your own study, or in your weekly Bible study group.
The ministry runs the track as workshop sessions over selected days. Each subject is taught in full, with time for questions.

caveat.ask: To arrange the training for yourself, your group or your ministry, speak to the Bible Study Committee.

vision.lead: Whoever teaches this school — a teacher from within the fellowship or a guest invited for a subject — teaches within these convictions. They are not preferences. They are what the curriculum was built on, and a teacher who will not hold them should not be given these classes.

items.d: Every track, every week, every class leads to Christ. A lesson that ends in a moral point, a personality or a programme has missed the aim.
Teach what the passage says where it stands. Let Scripture explain Scripture, and explain the connection rather than stacking references.
Salvation is God's free gift, received by faith and never earned. Holiness is the fruit of that gift, never its price.

items.t: No fear is used on the people
items.d: Curses, bloodlines, village powers and the fear of hidden forces are not teaching tools here. Christ has redeemed us, and a teacher who moves people by fear is not teaching this curriculum.
Testimony is welcome; doctrine comes from the Scriptures and the faith of the Church. No class is built on a vision, a dream or an encounter.
Every teacher shows how he reached his conclusion, takes questions, and can be checked against the open Bible. Anyone who cannot be asked a question does not teach here.
The purpose is to produce teachers who can teach others faithfully. A session that impressed people but formed nobody has failed.

vision.guest: Before a guest teacher is invited for any subject, the committee should ask three things: what he will teach, from which passages, and how he reaches his conclusions. A sound teacher answers all three gladly.
